result.summary: Demeter and Persephone are reunited, and Hecate becomes Persephone's companion. Zeus sends Rhea to settle the dispute: Persephone will spend a third of the year below and two thirds above. Demeter makes the earth fruitful again, teaches her mysteries to the princes of Eleusis, and the poet closes with a prayer.

scenes.title: Mother and daughter reunited
scenes.summary: Demeter and Persephone embrace and are comforted. Hecate joins them and becomes Persephone's companion.

scenes.title: Rhea brings Zeus's settlement
scenes.summary: Zeus sends Rhea, who meets Demeter on the plain of Rharus and relays his terms. Demeter yields and makes the earth fruitful.
scenes.stakes: Demeter risks losing her daughter for part of the year, and mankind risks famine unless she relents.

scenes.title: The mysteries taught
scenes.summary: Demeter teaches her rites to the Eleusinian kings and then returns to Olympus. The initiated are promised blessings and wealth.
scenes.stakes: The uninitiated face a bleak lot after death.

scenes.title: Poet's prayer
scenes.summary: The poet addresses Demeter and Persephone, asks for a livelihood, and promises another song.

alias_notes.explanation: An alternative name for Demeter used in the closing prayer.

notable_quotes.reason: Core statement of the Eleusinian Mysteries' promise of a better afterlife for initiates.

analysis.text: The compromise explains the seasons: Persephone's time below matches barren months, and her return brings spring and renewed grain.
The hymn is an origin story for the Eleusinian Mysteries, a secret initiation cult promising blessings in the afterlife.

legacy.text: The Eleusinian Mysteries continued for nearly two thousand years and influenced later ideas of initiation and the afterlife.

fun_facts.text: The word 'mystery' comes from Greek mystes, an initiate, and the secrecy of the rites was so well kept that details remain uncertain.

language_notes.text: "Bright-coiffed" means with beautifully dressed hair; "minister" here means attendant or servant.
"Third part of the circling year" means four months below, two-thirds above; this explains the seasons' cycle.
The Rharian plain near Eleusis was sacred to Demeter; she had made it barren in her anger at losing her daughter.
"Bowed his head in token" refers to a nod by which Zeus makes a promise binding.
"Transgress or pry into" means violate or inquire about; the mysteries were secret and could not be revealed.
Plutus is the personified god of wealth, often linked with Demeter's grain harvests.

context_notes.text: Hecate, a goddess associated with night and crossroads, heard Persephone's cry when she was seized and helped Demeter search.
Cronos was the Titan father of Zeus; Rhea is his wife and also Zeus's mother, so she speaks as Demeter's sister.
These Eleusinian kings were the legendary first priests of the Eleusinian Mysteries, a secret initiation cult in Demeter's honor.

literary_notes.text: The barren plain is told of as it will soon be, anticipating the harvest that will follow Demeter's reconciliation.
The blessed initiate is set against the uninitiate in death, stressing the value of the rites.
The poet turns directly to the goddess, using a string of epithets and places to honor her and ask for a reward.
